text.p: Britain's Inntrepeneur Pub Company Ltd, jointly owned by Foster's Brewing Group of Australia and Grand Metropolitan Plc, on Friday launched a package of discounts on the beers it supplies to its 3,000 tied pubs.
The discounts will be of at least 30 stg per barrel and will range up to 60 stg depending on the beer type and the volume bought by the pub, the company said in a statement.

Inntrepreneur currently provides mainstream brands to its pubs only from Scottish Courage, part of brewer Scottish & Newcastle Plc, but after the end of this contract in March 1998 the pub firm intends to widen its supplier base.

Friday's move, part of a package of measures to reorganise the competitive position of its tenants and lessees (which Inntrepreneur calls its retailers), follows the completion of a regulatory review of the company by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) earlier this week.
An Inntrepreneur spokesman said the package and the extra discounts, which will be directly funded by the company, were patently in line with the latest DTI ruling.

"We are now in a position to use our purchasing power and other resources to provide a a package of benefits to our retailers which will enable them to compete effectively and more profitably," the statement quoted chief executive Mark Foster as saying.
All the discounts will be backdated to January this year and are to be guaranteed until September 1998.
The company currently supplies about 800,000 barrels of beer per year and the spokesman said the company expected most of the retailers in its chain would take up the discounts.
He could not say, however, how much of the discount would be passed on over the counter to drinkers as this was up to the individual pub managers.

Analysts estimate that while Inntrepreneur tenants have in the past paid between 220 to 250 stg per barrel of standard lager, for example, many of their rival publicans supplied by other independents paid as much as 50 stg less.
